walkthroughs.body_html:
The Restless Earth — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Restless Earth brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Restless Earth.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The San Andreas Fault is what type of margin?
options: Constructive
Destructive
Conservative
Collision

mcqs.q: Are the continents fixed in place?
options: Continents move only during earthquakes.
The map of the continents has always looked the way it does now.
No — tectonic plates move a few centimetres a year, driven by mantle convection, slab pull and ridge push, slowly rearranging the oceans and continents.
Earthquakes are harmless if they happen at weekends.

mcqs.q: Do volcanoes only occur at plate boundaries?
options: Volcanoes grow from buried bonfires.
Earthquakes are harmless if they happen at weekends.
Mostly they do, but hot spots like Hawaii form volcanoes in plate interiors where plumes of hot mantle rise, so the boundary rule has important exceptions.
Every volcano sits exactly on a plate margin.

mcqs.q: Does a bigger earthquake always cause more deaths?
options: Earthquakes are harmless if they happen at weekends.
Magnitude alone determines an earthquake's death toll.
Volcanoes grow from buried bonfires.
No — impacts depend on depth, distance from population, building quality, preparedness and response; moderate quakes in vulnerable places can kill far more than great quakes in prepared ones.
